## My thinking this season

I've been growing cotton on these 13.1 mu for a long time now — 35 years of farming teaches you what works here in Quzhou. Cotton is what I know, and the land on the western side of our village suits it better than wheat-maize anyway. My husband and I handle most of the work, but two of our kids work in town now, so I only really have family help during busy times like picking.

Money is always tight. I can't throw fertilizer around like the big farms do. I usually put down compound fertilizer before planting — maybe one bag of 15-15-15 per mu as base, then topdress urea once when the cotton starts flowering. The extension station said last year we could cut nitrogen a bit, but I don't want to risk the yield — I'll stick with what worked. About 15 kg N per mu total feels right, same as usual.

I'll plant mid-April after the soil warms up, using the hybrid seed the agro-shop sells — it's Bt cotton so the bollworm problem is less bad than it used to be, but I still need to spray for aphids and mirid bugs. Herbicide before planting saves a lot of weeding labor. I'll irrigate twice from the well — once at bud stage if it's dry, and once at flowering-boll. The electricity for pumping adds up, so I don't irrigate more than I have to.

Picking is the hard part. 13.1 mu of cotton means a lot of picking days across three rounds. I'll hire a few neighbors for the peak picks and pay them by weight. If prices are okay this year — I heard cotton is around 7 yuan per jin of seed cotton — I should clear some money after inputs.
